# Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies Foundation

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-30 · status **complete** · Core profile fields covered from three years of audited annual reports and the funder's own site; CIN/PAN and an explicit application/RFP page were searched for and not found within budget.

Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies Foundation (RNPF) is a private, family-led grantmaking foundation registered as a Section 8 company under the Companies Act 2013, chaired by Rohini Nilekani (also founder of the separately-run Arghyam water/sanitation foundation and co-founder of Pratham Books/EkStep). It is not a corporate CSR arm. Confirmed via its own site and three annual reports (FY2022-23, FY2023-24, FY2024-25) as an active, growing grantmaker: total grants rose from Rs 30.7 Cr (43 grants, FY2022-23) to Rs 89 Cr programme spend (FY2023-24) to Rs 118.22 Cr across 155 partners (FY2024-25), with Rs 153 Cr / 407 grantees stated for the current FY2025-26 (in-progress, as posted on the live site). It funds a large number of named external NGOs directly (unrestricted, multi-year, organisational-support grants) across eight portfolios: Climate & Environment, Mental Health, Active Citizenship, Access to Justice, Laayak (gender/young men & boys), Ecosystem Building, Arts & Culture, and Research & Academia. No public RFP, eligibility criteria, or online application form was found; the funder's own materials describe a trust-based, relationship-driven, largely invitation-only model with unrestricted and multi-year grants rather than open calls. A single large named grant (INR 100 Crore, announced March 2023, to NIMHANS and NCBS jointly, to set up 'The Centre for Brain and Mind') was found as an example of grant-level disclosure. Explicit state/district-level footprint disclosure and a CIN/PAN were not found within budget.

Website: https://rohininilekaniphilanthropies.org

## What it set out to find

- identity: legal name, structure, relationship to Rohini Nilekani and Arghyam, website, entity type
- csr_year/spend: latest annual grantmaking figures and 2-3 prior years, FY tagged, as worded
- themes and geography: sectors/portfolios, states/districts where work ran vs stated priority geography
- whether they fund external NGOs: named grantees, project titles, amounts, years
- how to apply: grant size, eligibility, process, open/rolling/invitation-only, deadlines, contact
- evidence: annual reports, website, grantee lists, press, with URLs and quotes
